Clarity.justification: The paper is well-structured with clear sections (Introduction, Related Work, Methodology, Results, Discussion, Conclusion). The hypothesis, implementation details, gate criteria, and root-cause hierarchy are explicitly stated. Figures (ρ_j distributions, NLI heatmaps, autocorrelation plots) directly support the claims. Minor deduction for repetitive emphasis on the same core finding across sections.

Novelty.justification: The core technical observation (NLI models trained on SNLI/MNLI fail on factual verification) is already known in domain-adaptation literature. The contribution is primarily a systematic replication case study of CCP with concrete failure metrics (20-80× deviation in ρ_j) and an adapted reproducibility checklist (R1–R4). This is a useful negative-result contribution but not conceptually groundbreaking.

Soundness.justification: The experimental design is rigorous: the authors correctly diagnose that the NLI model was never validated on factual examples before hypothesis testing. Sanity checks on TruthfulQA correct/incorrect pairs, statistical tests (Wilcoxon, Cohen’s d), and the root-cause hierarchy (Tier 1: OOD generalization gap) are well-supported. Code artifacts (mock experiments, visualization scripts, checkpointing) enable reproduction of the failure. Minor deduction for reliance on a single NLI model without ablation of alternatives.

Significance.justification: The paper addresses a critical methodological issue—measurement validity must precede hypothesis testing—and provides concrete, adoptable recommendations (raw metric distributions, NLI calibration diagnostics). With 50+ hallucination papers citing NLI methods in 2024, documenting this failure mode has practical field-level value. The work is unlikely to have lasting theoretical impact but is significant for reproducibility standards.

strengths: Transparent documentation of a failed replication with quantitative evidence (ρ_j values 20-80× below expected range)
Clear methodological lesson and actionable reproducibility checklist (R1–R4) adapted from Dodge et al. (2019)
weaknesses: Core technical finding (NLI miscalibration for factual verification) is already documented in prior domain-adaptation literature
Limited novelty beyond the specific application to CCP; no new method or theoretical insight is proposed
